# `prefer-write-byte`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: fix all · Options: none

Reports writing a single character via `writeAll` or `print` on a writer,
recommending `writeByte` instead.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

`writer.print` parses format strings, decodes flags, and inspects tuple types at
runtime. `writer.writeAll` verifies slice lengths and loops through memory
chunks. When writing a single character or byte, `writer.writeByte` writes
directly to the destination stream or buffer with no formatting or slice
machinery.

## When it fires

```zig
// Inefficient: slice iteration or runtime format string parsing
try writer.writeAll("}");
try writer.print("\n", .{});
try writer.print("{c}", .{ch});

// Fast: single byte write directly into the stream buffer
try writer.writeByte('}');
try writer.writeByte('\n');
try writer.writeByte(ch);
```

The rule reports: 1. `writer.writeAll("c")` with 1-character string literals. 2.
`writer.print("c", .{})` with 1-character string literals and empty argument
tuples. 3. `writer.print("{c}", .{ch})` with single character arguments.
Multi-byte strings and complex format expressions are ignored.

The receiver must plausibly be a writer. Namespace functions such as
`std.debug.print` (which has no `writeByte`), receivers declared with a type
other than a writer (a project's own `*Buffer` with a `print` method), and a
call passed straight to another call, as in
`expectError(error.WriteFailed, w.writeAll("x"))`, are not reported. A
receiver whose type is unknown (an `anytype` parameter, a field, a call result)
counts only when its name says it is a writer: it contains `writer`, `stdout`
or `stderr`, or is `w`, `bw`, `out`, `output`, `out_stream` or `interface`.
`check --fix` applies the rewrite only when the receiver is declared as
`std.Io.Writer` or a pointer to it; for an `anytype` parameter, a field or
another writer type, it stays an editor quick fix.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn newline(writer: *std.Io.Writer) !void {
    try writer.writeAll("\n");
}
```
